summary: The report must not receive independent-review clearance. Its absence pipeline manufactures per-edge passing executions from one categorical barrier test, including 4,692 live-reachability obligations with no edge-specific descriptor probe. The teardown corpus also does not prove the fixture plan's post-destruction callback, completion, event, Host-context, timer, and native-handle requirements.

findings.title: Absence evidence synthesizes 14,304 per-edge passes without per-edge source and live probes
evidence: src/host/embedder_artifacts.rs:3100-3344 runs one runtime and one shared barrier, then unconditionally emits passed source-install and live-reachability observations for all 7,152 structurally absent edges.

Only 2,460 edges receive descriptor-path probes. The committed absence artifact contains 4,692 passed live-reachability observations whose proof.descriptorPrefixes is empty, including builtin:assert, builtin:fs, builtin:crypto, loaders, CLI surfaces, callbacks, startup paths, and Host ABI edges.
The source-install proof merely copies implementationBranches from the generated implementation manifest; it performs no per-edge install-route or call-graph closure analysis.

packages/ibex-devtools/src/scripts/restricted-exact-absence-evidence.mjs:247-283 accepts empty descriptorPrefixes whenever the root-global manifest has no entry and checks copied metadata rather than an executed source-closure result.

packages/ibex-devtools/src/scripts/restricted-exact-absence-evidence.mjs:307-322 expands every observation from the single command into a distinct fixture and execution. This contradicts its target-report invariant that broad command success never synthesizes per-edge passes and violates LLP 0033's fixture-specific absence requirements.
findings.recommendation: Invalidate all affected structurally-absent rows. Generate an explicit probe plan for every edge covering installers, aliases, lazy resolution, imports, callbacks, retained closures, and attacker-reachable roots. Source-install rows must carry independently checked closure results, and live rows with no executable probe plan must remain missing or failed. Do not expand a shared command into per-edge executions unless its output contains independently verified, edge-specific observations.

findings.title: The teardown corpus is credited without testing the required post-destruction lifecycle boundaries
evidence: capsec/registry/restricted-exact-fixture-plan.json requires proof that no callback, completion, event binding, Host context, timer, or native handle remains callable or reusable after destruction.
packages/ibex-devtools/src/scripts/run-restricted-exact-global-corpora.mjs:43-48 maps teardown to three tests whose success is recognized only through generic cargo markers.

The control-plane test checks only that ibex_test_runtime_registered changes from 1 to 0 around ex_hermes_destroy. Its recorded refusal text claims Host-context teardown without probing context reuse or outstanding producers.
The two checkpoint-failure tests perform poison/refusal checks before destruction and then call ex_hermes_destroy; they make no post-destruction observation.

The implementation contains queue draining and native-worker pin logic, but the committed evidence does not exercise an in-flight teardown race or establish suppression/refusal for callbacks, completions, events, timers, Host contexts, or native handles.
findings.recommendation: Keep the teardown corpus incomplete. Add synchronized race fixtures that hold each producer class in flight while teardown enters Closing, verify admitted work drains without user-code delivery, verify late generation-scoped callbacks and completions are rejected, verify event/timer/native handles cannot be reused, and verify the released Host context cannot be re-entered or confused with a later runtime generation.
